title: Assembly of a renal countercurrent system in a beetle
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Countercurrent exchange describes the crossover of some property between two bodies flowing in opposite direction. Countercurrent circuits, which work more efficiently than concurrent circuits, are common in nature and mimicked in human engineering. An example is the beetle cryptonephridial complex (CNC)—a multi-organ water conservation system which makes key contributions to the water budget in a vast number of species. It is even used by some to harvest water from the atmosphere. The system evolved by a radical reorganisation of insect internal anatomy bringing the renal/Malpighian tubules and rectum into countercurrent configuration, and their isolation in a chamber by an unusual tissue of unknown origin—the perinephric membrane. The CNC is richly supplied with tracheae to meet the high metabolic demands of the system. How the CNC is assembled during development is unknown. Here we characterise CNC development in the model beetle Tribolium castaneum and discover the molecular signals orchestrating its assembly. We find that dynamic crosstalk between the developing precursor cells of the rectum, Malpighian tubules, perinephric membrane, and trachea rely on a single, differentially spliced fibroblast growth factor (FGF) receptor and two FGF pathway ligands. We also map the origin of the perinephric membrane to a previously uncharacterised population of mesodermal cells, providing clues to its evolutionary origin. This work illuminates the developmental processes underpinning the reorganisation of the insect internal body plan to assemble a natural countercurrent system, one which is fundamental to beetle physiology, ecology and evolutionary success.

title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-contaminated wastewater into value-added ammonium products offers a promising pathway, yet practical implementation is hindered by sluggish nitrate reduction kinetics and poor redox rate matching in paired electrolysis systems. Here we report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that enables kinetically synchronized nitrate reduction and sulfate oxidation for the direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate ((NH4)2S2O8). In situ spectroscopic measurements and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations show that the PdP2@Cu3P heterointerface catalyst dynamically shuttles active hydrogen from hydrogen-generation sites to nitrate-activation sites, revealing rapid P-mediated hydrogenation at the interface, thereby decoupling hydrogen production from consumption and bypassing the multistep proton-coupled electron transfer pathway. The catalyst achieves a nitrate reduction rate of 8.94 × 10⁻7 mol cm⁻2 s⁻1, an ammonia Faradaic efficiency exceeding 92%, and sustained operation at 220 mA cm⁻2. In a membrane-electrode paired electrolyzer, the system produces (NH4)2S2O8 at a rate of 1.6 mmol h⁻1 cm⁻2, with 55% lower energy consumption and ~99.6% lower CO2 emissions than conventional routes. This work establishes a general strategy for nitrate–sulfate wastewater valorization and high-value oxidant production.

title: Directly visualizing the energy level structure of quantum dot molecules
source: Nature Communications
abstract: The orbital, spin and valley degrees of freedom in silicon quantum dots (QDs) support many modes of spin qubit operation. However, it is generally challenging to probe the energy level spectrum over a large parameter space. We demonstrate a spectroscopic technique capable of mapping the energy level structure of a double quantum dot as a function of level detuning, interdot tunnel coupling, and magnetic field. In the one-electron regime, we directly observe the transition from the atom-like energy levels of isolated QDs to molecular-like bonding and anti-bonding states with increasing interdot tunnel coupling. We also resolve the Zeeman splitting of ground and excited valley states in a magnetic field. In the two-electron regime, we gain access to the detuning dependent singlet-triplet splitting. Our work may be extended to a broader class of systems, such as strong spin-orbit materials or proximitized QDs, allowing the direct extraction of various energy gaps.

title: Cytotoxic drugs and bispecific T cell engagers synergize to rewire host immunity and elicit polyclonal antitumor T cell responses
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Cytotoxic therapies such as chemotherapy and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) kill tumor cells directly but are limited by resistance, dose-limiting toxicity, and failure to induce durable antitumor immunity. Here we show that tumor-associated antigen (TAA)-targeted CD28 bispecific antibodies (TAAxCD28) convert cytotoxic agents into drivers of durable antitumor immunity. In humanized mouse models, combining the HER2-directed ADC trastuzumab deruxtecan (Tras-DXd) with TAAxCD28 antibodies enhances tumor rejection and promotes durable immune memory in Tras-DXd-resistant cancers, and comparable synergy is observed with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). This therapeutic strategy allows lower or less frequent cytotoxic drug dosing, potentially limiting systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, TAAxCD28 antibodies promote the activation and expansion of clonally-restricted tumor CD8+ T cells, and adding ADCs or chemotherapy sustains this activation while preserving a naïve/stem-like pool of tumor-specific CD8+ T cells with a diversified T cell receptor repertoire. Each cytotoxic agent supports this T cell activity through a separate innate mechanism: Tras-DXd expands and activates conventional dendritic cells, whereas 5-FU reprograms suppressive myeloid cells toward an immunostimulatory phenotype. Together, these findings support pairing cytotoxic agents with TAAxCD28 bispecifics to overcome resistance and improve long-term tumor control in refractory cancers.

title: Materials Control of Nitric Oxide in Cancer Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Nitric oxide (NO) can suppress antitumor immunity, support tumor adaptation, or promote immune‐mediated killing, making its therapeutic manipulation highly dependent on exposure. This Review examines how materials control NO source, localization, release kinetics, and chemical fate in cancer immunotherapy, with particular attention to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). We analyze polymeric donors, nanocarriers, injectable depots, and strategies for restricting endogenous NO production, linking their physicochemical properties to target exposure and immune function. Evidence from checkpoint‐treated models is distinguished from mechanisms established with other therapies and from human associations. Comparative analyses separate donor capacity from measured NO exposure, carrier accumulation from cellular delivery, and distant‐tumor control from demonstrated immune memory. Four overlapping endogenous contexts, comprising tumor adaptation, myeloid suppression, vascular dysfunction, and inflammatory effector activity, guide intervention design without constituting validated patient categories. We identify testable predictions concerning cellular selectivity, release kinetics, and spatial pharmacodynamic responses. Translation requires measurements that connect material behavior to a defined NO‐dependent process while demonstrating preservation of beneficial endothelial and immune functions. This framework provides a basis for evaluating when localized NO delivery or selective inhibition may support ICB, while recognizing the limits of current preclinical and clinical evidence.

title: Non‐Precious Metal High‐Entropy Oxide Sub‐1 nm Nanowires for Li‐O2 Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Highly active and structurally robust cathode catalysts are critically required to boost the electrochemical performance of lithium‐oxygen batteries (LOBs). Herein, a generally synthetic method of non‐precious metal high‐entropy oxide‐polyoxometalate sub‐1 nm nanowires (NPMHEO‐POM SNWs) has been successfully developed induced by POM clusters under mild solvothermal conditions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal that the dominantly driving forces for the assembly of POMs and multi‐metal oxides are the Coulomb and van der Waals forces, enabling precise theoretical guidance for targeted material synthesis. Benefiting from the 1D ultrafine structure with fully exposed active sites, the precise adjustment of components optimizing the adsorption capability of intermediate (LiO
                    2
                    *) and discharge product (Li
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    ), and the strong interactions of multi‐metal oxides and POMs contributing to the stability, the BiVZrNiCeO
                    x
                    ‐phosphomolybdic acid SNWs‐based LOB achieves a highly specific capacity of 9944 mAh g
                    −1
                    and stable cycling durability for 312 cycles at 500 mA g
                    −1
                    , highlighting their great promise as high‐efficiency electrocatalysts for advanced LOBs.

title: Ultra‐Stable Phosphide Barrier Layer for Thermoelectric Bismuth Telluride
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The long‐term reliability of bismuth telluride (BT) thermoelectric power generation devices is severely constrained by the lack of reliable barrier layers. In this work, Ni
                    2
                    P is proposed as an ultra‐stable barrier layer for N‐type BT (N–BT). The low thermodynamic driving force for interfacial reaction and the sluggish Ni migration in Ni
                    2
                    P together ensure the favorable chemical inertness of the Ni
                    2
                    P/N–BT interface, while atomic‐scale bonding endows the interface with high bonding energy, leading to the lowest interfacial contact resistivity (∼1 µΩ cm
                    2
                    ), highest bonding strength (∼20 MPa), and longest verified stable duration at 523 K (90 days) among reported barrier layer systems. The resulting seven‐pair BT thermoelectric device achieves a maximum energy conversion efficiency of 6.9% at a temperature difference of 230 K. This work not only addresses the long‐standing bottleneck in power generation applications of BT‐based devices since the 1950s, but also provides guidance for barrier layer design in other thermoelectric systems.

title: Topological Superlattice Stabilized Layered Oxide Cathodes With Sustainable Anionic Redox
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Harnessing the oxygen anionic redox (OAR) at high voltage is envisaged as a fascinating approach to promote the energy density of rechargeable batteries. However, the layered transition metal (TM) oxide cathode materials with OAR activity suffer severely from detrimental phase transformations and local structural disorders, leading to electrochemical performance degradation. Herein, we propose a topological superlattice regulation strategy to construct a cathode material with the Li/Mg/Ni‐triple‐center honeycomb superlattice for sodium‐ion batteries. The combined theoretical and in/ex situ investigations demonstrate that the Li/Mg‐centered superlattice topology activates the OAR reaction to boost specific capacity, while the Ni‐centered honeycomb motif prevents the lattice oxygen release by increasing the TM−O covalency. Furthermore, the multi‐topology superlattice configuration suppresses the P−O phase transition and Li/TM interlayer/intralayer migration to reinforce the honeycomb superstructure stability, improving the oxygen redox reversibility. Consequently, the topological superlattice‐stabilized cathode delivers a high capacity of 242 mAh g
                    −1
                    and exhibits outstanding cycling stability (91.8% capacity retention after 100 cycles). This work provides new insights into the superstructure regulation of state‐of‐the‐art cathode materials for sustainable batteries.

title: Quicklime Slaking‐Mediated Exothermic Reactions in Polidocanol‐Integrated Ablators with Inhibited Heat Diffusion Enable Cancer Thermal Ablation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Despite showing a wide application in tumor therapy, the clinically‐used exogenous thermal ablation still suffers from uncontrollable temperature field with rapid heat diffusion. Here an endogenous trigger‐encouraged thermal ablation, namely exothermic reaction‐based thermal ablation (ERTA) based on quicklime slaking and acid‐base neutralization reactions, has been established, wherein CaO nanoparticles were encapsulated with Ag nanoparticles by liposomes to construct ERTA ablators. CaO consumes H
                    2
                    O and H
                    +
                    after exothermic reactions to give birth to Ca
                    2+
                    and heat. Liposome shell prolongs ERTA via limiting the exothermic reaction rate, and intracellular Ca
                    2+
                    overload unites with Ag nanoparticles to produce antitumor ROS to boost cancer ERTA. Importantly, polidocanol‐based foam sclerosing agent (PFSA) with low heat conductivity was integrated to inhibit heat diffusion and confine heat in tumor to elevate temperature and enhance ERTA efficiency. Additionally, PFSA as a routine clinical embolism agent destroys intratumoral blood vessels to occlude blood vessels and establish starvation therapy, which further improves PFSA‐enhanced ERTA efficiency. Consequently, such ERTA‐based ablators and PFSA‐integrated ones outperform the scale‐matched microwave ablation and laboratory‐in photothermal ablation in repressing subcutaneous and orthotopic hepatocellular carcinoma, and orthotopic pancreatic cancer. This endogenous trigger‐activated thermal ablation method provides distinctive insights into thermal ablation, presenting a new thermal ablation protocol.

title: An In Situ Amorphous Thermoconversion Strategy for Macroscopic Glass Heterojunctions
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Heterojunction fabrication has long been constrained by the stringent lattice‐matching requirements between dissimilar components, limiting the accessible material combinations and processing routes. Here, we report an amorphous thermoconversion strategy for constructing hybrid glass heterojunctions in situ. In this approach, structural competition among liquid phases derived from distinct metal–organic hybrid halide crystal structures generates divergent luminescence across amorphous phases, giving rise to a new family of halide glass heterojunctions. These hybrid halide glasses display excitation‐dependent and time‐gated persistent luminescence that is color‐tunable across a 160 nm wavelength window, a property that enables direct optical visualization and confers broad photonic versatility. Beyond their optical attributes, the resulting macroscopic glass heterojunctions exhibit well‐defined mechanical rigidity and arbitrary processability, supporting spatially resolved fluorescence and persistent luminescence outputs alongside one‐dimensional (1D) optical waveguiding at losses that surpass those of state‐of‐the‐art crystalline counterparts. Therefore, this work delivers the demonstration of macroscopic heterojunctions in halide supramolecular glasses and establishes a scalable route to multi‐channel, low‐dimensional optical waveguide for information storage and encryption applications.

title: Anionic Lone‐Pair‐Like Electrons Induced Ultra‐Low Lattice Thermal Conductivity and High Thermoelectric Performance
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The traditional lone‐pair electron strategy primarily reduces lattice thermal conductivity (
                    κ
                    L
                    ) by enhancing anharmonic lattice vibrations. However, this mechanism has long been considered to exist only in specific cations with ns
                    2
                    electron configurations (e.g. Sb
                    3+
                    , Bi
                    3+
                    ), severely restricting the broader applicability of this lone‐pair‐based approach. In this study, CuInSnSe
                    4
                    is successfully synthesized via atomic cross‐substitution from the diamondoid CuInSe
                    2
                    , wherein the Se atoms exhibit an anionic lone‐pair‐like electronic behavior, revealing a new approach to reducing
                    κ
                    L
                    that differs from conventional cation‐based mechanisms. In contrast to the traditional mechanism that relies on cations to enhance lattice anharmonicity, the anionic lone‐pair electrons weaken the Se‐Se interactions, flatten the optical phonon branches, and consequently significantly expand the scattering phase space, providing more scattering channels for phonons. This anionic lone‐pair electron strategy reduces the room‐temperature
                    κ
                    L
                    from 4.48 to 1.26 W m
                    −1
                    K
                    −1
                    . Ultimately, the predicted optimal thermoelectric figure of merit (
                    ZT
                    ) for p‐type and n‐type CuInSnSe
                    4
                    attains values of 1.99 and 0.79, respectively. This work systematically expands the conventional application boundaries of the lone‐pair electron strategy and elucidates a fundamentally distinct mechanism for
                    κ
                    L
                    reduction, providing a new theoretical basis for designing and developing novel high‐efficiency thermoelectric materials with intrinsically low
                    κ

title: Revisiting the Role of Dynamic Linkages in Polymer Compatibilization Using Diazirine–Anhydride Conjugates
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Small‐molecule crosslinkers can compatibilize mixed plastics through reactive extrusion, providing a potential solution to extant challenges in polymer recycling. Existing studies have prioritized the use of crosslinker molecules that incorporate dynamic linkages between reactive warheads; however, the absolute requirement for these dynamic groups remains unproven, and previous comparisons of static versus dynamic crosslinkers employed molecules with vastly different C–H insertion efficiencies. In this study, we employed chemistry‐explicit reaction molecular dynamics simulations, small‐molecule surrogates of interface reactions, phase morphology studies, and mechanical analysis to explicitly test hypotheses around the value of dynamic linkages. Using rationally designed, reactivity‐matched pairs of dynamic and static crosslinkers, we found the presence of dynamic anhydride linkages did not generally improve compatibilization efficacy. Instead, dynamic exchange enabled reorganization of compatibilizing hetero‐crosslinks into non‐compatibilizing homo‐crosslinks over time, while facilitating other undesirable reactivity pathways. Our findings indicate compatibilization performance is dictated by physicochemical control over crosslinker distribution, rather than dynamic bonding, and that the kinetics of dynamic exchange must be tightly regulated to avoid undermining compatibilization. We anticipate that these findings will guide the development of improved crosslinker reagents for polymer compatibilization and other materials applications.

title: One Carbon Matters: Conformational Bending Stabilizes Ferroelectric Nematic Order and Enables Domain‐Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic C Order
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Molecular design of ferroelectric nematics has primarily focused on optimizing highly polar rigid mesogenic cores, whereas the role of flexible aliphatic segments in regulating molecular conformation and polar ordering remains insufficiently understood. Here, we show that exchanging the positions of a methylene group and the ether oxygen within the linkage between a polar rigid core and an aliphatic tail (Ar‐O‐CH
                    2
                    ‐ versus Ar‐CH
                    2
                    ‐O‐) reshapes the molecular conformational landscape and profoundly influences the stability of the ferroelectric nematic (N
                    F
                    ) phase. Molecules with a stronger preference for bent, pear‐like effective geometries exhibit significantly enhanced N
                    F
                    stability, accompanied by reduced splay and bend elastic constants in the apolar nematic phase, and lower apparent activation barriers for dipolar reorientation. Further elongation of the flexible segment introduces competing packing motifs and gives rise to a domain‐modulated antiferroelectric smectic C (SmC
                    AF
                    ) phase. These findings establish conformational bending as a molecular‐shape parameter for controlling hierarchical ferroelectric and antiferroelectric liquid‐crystalline order, bridging the design principles of conventional bent‐core layered ferroelectrics with emerging rod‐like fluid ferroelectric materials.

title: Photo‐Induced Multi‐Physical Field Synergy for Direct Natural Seawater Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Direct natural seawater electrolysis offers a sustainable route for green hydrogen production, yet severe performance degradation stemming from irreversible interfacial precipitation hinders its practical application. Herein, a photo‐induced multi‐physical field synergy strategy is developed to dynamically regulate interfacial OH
                    −
                    transfer and eliminate cathode pH self‐amplifying polarization. A plasmonic photo‐responsive electrode constructed via ultrathin amorphous MoO
                    3
                    coating on PtMo alloy nanoparticles is fabricated to integrate photo‐induced asymmetric electric field (PAEF) and localized photothermal field (PLPF). Such a well‐designed core‐shell structure delivers a record‐high industrial current density of 8 A cm
                    −2
                    at low overpotential (433 mV) in alkaline seawater. In situ characterizations and spectroscopic analyses verify that the dual fields optimize the electric double‐layer ion distribution and drive microscale thermal convection, accelerating OH
                    −
                    dissipation. Benefiting from the above, the engineered light‐responsive catalytic system exhibits a low overpotential of 232 mV at 100 mA cm
                    −2
                    in natural seawater, alongside anti‐precipitation ability, and maintains stable operation over 100 h (6.2% decay). A photo‐assisted asymmetric electrolyzer achieves a low cell voltage of 2.27 V at 0.5 A cm
                    −2
                    for seawater splitting, which realizes effective green hydrogen generation under fluctuating natural solar light (normalized ramp‐following ratio > 0.9).

title: A Phosphonium Relay for Integrated Cleavage‐to‐Cyclization of Cyclic Peptides
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Head‐to‐tail macrocyclization of peptides is typically performed through stepwise workflows that separate resin cleavage, isolation of linear intermediates, and subsequent cyclization, largely due to incompatible activation requirements for each transformation. Here we report a phosphonium‐mediated relay that unifies these steps within a single activation node. In this design, an electrophile‐activated phosphonium species promotes cleavage from standard 2‐chlorotrityl chloride (2‐CTC) resin and is proposed to enable in situ formation of a
                    C
                    ‐terminally activated intermediate for intramolecular amidation. The strategy directly couples cleavage to cyclization on standard peptide supports without auxiliary linkers, intermediate purification, or high‐dilution cyclization conditions. The method is compatible with diverse peptide sequccnces and functional handles and can be integrated into a closed‐loop automated workflow for end‐to‐end synthesis, with advantages for hydrophobic substrates by avoiding isolation of poorly soluble linear intermediates such as
                    Vespid chemotactic peptide 5f
                    . Process‐level benchmarking against side‐chain anchoring further demonstrated favorable process metrics and gram‐scale scalability. This work establishes a linker‐free cleavage‐to‐cyclization strategy and provides a practical framework for integrated and automation‐compatible cyclic peptide synthesis.

title: Robust Tetrazine‐Bridged Binuclear Iridium(III) Complex Featuring Tunable Conformational Dynamics for Efficient Photothermal Conversion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Developing near‐infrared photothermal materials with outstanding conversion efficiency and high photostability remains a critical challenge for small‐molecule systems. We report a unique donor‐acceptor platform based on a binuclear iridium(III) architecture featuring a bridging electron‐deficient 1,2,4,5‐tetrazine ligand. The complex exhibits strong and broad absorption up to 1200 nm in solution and 1500 nm in the solid state, significantly outperforming other metal complexes. Temperature‐ and solvent‐dependent
                    1
                    H NMR coupled with X‐ray diffraction suggest the ‘butterfly‐like’ conformational behavior of the complex, while theoretical calculations identify low‐energy charge‐transfer transitions from cyclometalated cores to the tetrazine moiety as the origin of the exceptionally high absorbance and efficient non‐radiative relaxation. This facilitates robust photothermal activity across three different excitation wavelengths (635, 808, 980 nm), delivering an excellent conversion efficiency of 94.9% at 808 nm (acetone solvate) along with long‐term stability over multiple cycles (CHCl
                    3
                    /CH
                    2
                    Cl
                    2
                    ‐derived phase), uniquely tunable through crystal packing engineering. When applied to cellulose paper, the complex drives solar‐to‐thermal water evaporation with an efficiency of 86.6%. This high performance is accompanied by exceptional photostability under prolonged irradiation, ranking the developed material among the most competitive systems reported. Overall, this work establishes bridging 1,2,4,5‐tetrazines and crystal engineering as powerful tools for designing high‐performance organometallic photothermal materials.

title: Photocatalytic Disruption of Concurrent Redox Axes Elicits Convergent Redox Collapse
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The interconnected antioxidant systems of cancer cells, centered on the glutathione and thioredoxin axes, constitute a promising therapeutic vulnerability. However, simultaneous disruption of both axes by dual‐inhibitor regimens is hampered by pharmacokinetic asynchrony. Herein, we report squaraine‐based photocatalysts as a single‐agent modality that concurrently disrupts these interconnected antioxidant systems in cancer cells. Upon 635 nm light irradiation,
                    IITC
                    depletes intracellular NADPH and GSH through photocatalytic oxidation coupled with type I/II photosensitization. NADPH depletion deprives the reductive coenzyme of thioredoxin reductase in the thioredoxin axis, while glutathione oxidation collapses the central antioxidant axis. Consequently,
                    IITC
                    ablates both antioxidant axes concurrently and exerts potent phototherapeutic anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, during phototherapy
                    IITC
                    undergoes self‐immolation into nontoxic degraded fragments, thereby avoiding phototoxicity post‐treatment. This self‐eliminating, metabolism‐targeted photocatalytic strategy establishes a new avenue for safe and efficient cancer phototherapy.

title: Spatial Electrostatic Complementarity in MOF Pores Enables Selective Recognition of Closely Related Fluoromethanes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Trace purification of chemically similar gases is particularly challenging when molecular size and kinetics offer little contrast and conventional affinity descriptors provide conflicting guidance. Trifluoromethane (CHF
                    3
                    ) removal from monofluoromethane (CH
                    3
                    F) exemplifies this problem: CH
                    3
                    F has the greater dipole moment, and CHF
                    3
                    is more polarizable. Here, to our knowledge, we report the first adsorptive removal of trace CHF
                    3
                    from CH
                    3
                    F and demonstrate electrostatic complementary recognition (ECR) in interpenetrated anion‐pillared MOF pores. Localized, directional negative‐potential sites from TiF
                    6
                    2–
                    pillars and surrounding electropositive pyridyl C─H domains complement the 1H/3F electrostatic pattern of CHF
                    3
                    while geometrically frustrating the inverse 3H/1F pattern of CH
                    3
                    F. All other benchmark adsorbents showed an overall preference for CH
                    3
                    F, whereas both TIFSIX frameworks achieved a reversal of adsorption preference toward CHF
                    3
                    under trace‐relevant conditions. TIFSIX‐Cu‐dpt, featuring a more focused and directional ECR environment, adsorbed 18.5 cm
                    3
                    /g of CHF
                    3
                    at 0.1 kPa. Neutron diffraction, adsorption thermodynamics, and molecular simulations support a spatially complementary multipoint binding mode. Fixed‐bed breakthrough of a binary feed containing 1000 ppm CHF
                    3
                    produced CH
                    3
                    F with >99.999% purity relative to CHF
                    3
                    at 320 L/kg. These results show how spatial electrostatic complementarity can translate subtle molecular differences beyond conventional scalar descriptors into selective adsorption.

title: Trigonal Prismatic Coordination Field‐Induced d‐Orbital Splitting Enables σ Electron Activation for Efficient Polysulfide Conversion in Li–S Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Understanding the electron‐transfer pathways and the mechanism in facilitating polysulfide conversion is crucial for the rational design of catalysts in lithium–sulfur batteries. Herein, we designed an NbSe
                    2
                    model catalyst to investigate the electron‐transfer pathways at sublayer transition metal cation sites through coordination field modulation, and revealed the relationship between electron transfer and catalytic efficiency. Moreover, the
                    σ
                    *–
                    σ
                    and
                    π
                    *–
                    σ
                    electron transfer channels at transition metal sites are identified in terms of the coordination field theory and hybrid orbital theory, where the
                    σ
                    *–
                    σ
                    channel exhibits higher electron transfer efficiency and therefore enhances the adsorption and conversion role of transition metal sites in polysulfides. The designed trigonal prismatic NbSe
                    2
                    exhibits a reversible capacity up to 799 mAh g
                    −1
                    at a high rate of 5 C, and the battery maintains stability under ultra‐high sulfur loading, achieving a capacity retention rate as high as 95.85%. From an electronic perspective, this work reveals the role of coordination fields on catalytic activity, providing new insights for the rational design of catalysts in metal–S batteries.

title: Mixed-dimensional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology for high-performance integrated circuits
source: Nature Electronics
abstract: Low-dimensional semiconductors, such as one-dimensional carbon nanotubes and two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides, could be used to build scaled, energy-efficient electronic devices. However, although these materials can exhibit excellent unipolar device performance, complementary integration with balanced performance and low power consumption remains a challenge. Here we report a mixed-dimensional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology that combines two-dimensional single-crystal molybdenum disulfide n-type transistors and one-dimensional aligned carbon nanotube p-type transistors. We integrate enhancement-mode top-gate transistors with symmetric threshold voltages using a hard mask technology and pre-deposition annealing process. We use the approach to create complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor inverters that exhibit rail-to-rail operation with a peak static power of less than 1 pW and a single-stage delay of 19 ps. We also fabricate 180-nm-node area-equivalent static random-access memory that offers robust read–write operations with a noise margin of 22% and 40% operating voltage. The uniformity of the transistors and inverters also allows us to create basic logic gates and a 4-bit full adder.

title: Exciton-phonon interaction suppression enables efficient near-infrared perovskite quantum dot LEDs
source: Matter
abstract: In energy-transfer light emitters, lattice vibrations can drain energy before recombination and reduce near-infrared emission efficiency. This study uses an ion-pair treatment to change the surface of Yb-doped perovskite quantum dots, which reduces vibration-related losses and improves energy transfer. The resulting devices produce efficient, bright near-infrared light under electrical operation. The findings suggest that controlling lattice dynamics through surface chemistry can improve this dual-channel emitter.

title: Brønsted/Lewis acid-catalyzed divergent cascade cyclization of alkoxyallene for the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are two types of biogenetically related polycyclic monoterpenoid alkaloids with distinct structural features. Reported synthetic strategies typically construct the core architectures of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids independently, and no protocol enabling their simultaneous synthesis has yet been developed. Herein, we describe the assembly of both eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloid skeletons from a common alkoxyallene precursor, a characteristic that aligns with their inherent biogenetic connection. Our investigations reveal that upon Prins-type spirocyclization of the alkoxyallene under Brønsted or Lewis acid catalysis, the intermediate undergoes two discrete tandem reaction pathways: Mannich-like cyclization/migration to construct the skeleton of eburnane alkaloids under Brønsted acid catalysis, whereas nucleophilic addition to the indole iminium assembles the aspidofractinine alkaloids framework under Lewis acid catalysis. The developed divergent cascade cyclization strategy has been successfully applied to the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids including (−)-eburnamonine, (−)-eburnamenine, (+)-eburnamine, and (±)-aspidofractinine.

title: Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core
source: Nature
abstract: Gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication. Following entry into the cytoplasm, the poxvirus core dissociates from the lateral bodies and undergoes expansion, functioning as a compartment for early transcription1. However, how molecules are exchanged between the viral core and the host cytoplasm remains poorly understood. Here, using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging, we determine the structures of the portal complex and its central pore on the vaccinia virus core at 6.7 Å and 4.4 Å resolution, respectively. Guided by structural predictions and experimental density, we identify three viral proteins, E8, E6 and L3, as the principal components of the pore and construct a structural model of their organization. The pore contains a narrow, positively charged constriction formed by conserved lysine residues in L3, substitutions of which impair viral gene expression and propagation. The dimensions and electrostatic properties of the channel are consistent with a potential role in molecular exchange across the core wall. Together, our findings establish a structural framework for understanding the organization and potential function of the poxvirus portal complex.

title: A bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an aromatic cyclopentadienide ring
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Five-membered rings are ubiquitous in non-planar π systems, yet they are typically neutral, non-aromatic or anti-aromatic. Here we report the synthesis and characterization of pentabenzocorannulenide (PBC−), a bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an anionic, aromatic cyclopentadienide (Cp−) ring. The five-membered Cp− ring is generated quantitatively by aromatization-driven nucleophilic dealkylation (C–C bond cleavage) of a pentabenzocorannulene derivative. Through single crystal X-ray diffraction and quantum chemical analyses, we reveal the unique structural features and physicochemical properties of PBC−, demonstrating uncommon bonding pattern and electronic characteristics distinct from corannulene, fullerenes, end caps of carbon nanotubes and other geodesic polyarenes. PBC− has an exceptionally strong conjugate acid, undergoes reversible covalent functionalization and engages in η5-type metal complexation. Incorporating the iconic Cp− ring into a fully conjugated sp2 carbon network opens avenues for exploring non-conventional π systems.

title: Unlocking sustainable thermoelectric generation with zinc antimonide
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Thermoelectric technologies offer a compelling path to sustainable waste-heat recovery, yet their widespread deployment is constrained by the reliance of many high-performing materials on scarce, environmentally problematic, or expensive elements. Beyond maximizing conversion efficiency (η), practical thermoelectrics must reconcile performance with resource availability, environmental impact and economic cost. Here we establish zinc antimonide (ZnSb) as a cost-effective and sustainable thermoelectric material by benchmarking elemental abundance, raw-material cost and device efficiency. By leveraging dynamically activated carrier modulation and intrinsically low thermal conductivity, ZnSb achieves impressive material performance while avoiding reliance on scarce, costly, or environmentally problematic elements. Furthermore, we demonstrate a ZnSb-Mg3Sb1.5Bi0.5 device yielding a maximum η of 8% at ΔT = 400 K. This translates to a high efficiency-to-cost ratio of ~0.2% US$−1 kg, highlighting the unusual combination of performance and resource compatibility. Our findings provide a framework for evaluating thermoelectric materials beyond isolated record efficiencies towards scalable and sustainable energy harvesting.

title: Assessing the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centres
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: The rapid proliferation of hyperscale data centres (HDCs) in the USA—mainly driven by the adoption of artificial intelligence—has raised concerns about this industry’s carbon footprint. We compiled facility-level information on 403 US hyperscale data centres operating between May 2024 and April 2025 and estimated their electricity consumption, electricity sources and attributable CO2 emissions. Across facility-load scenarios, these HDCs consumed approximately 68–99 TWh of electricity and were associated with approximately 21–31 million metric tons of CO2 under a location-based, total-output balancing-authority attribution method. Under the central scenario, HDC electricity demand was approximately 82 TWh, corresponding to about 1.8% of total US electricity consumption, and attributable CO2 emissions were approximately 25.7 Mt. Roughly 54% of attributed generation was supplied by fossil-fuel sources. The HDC electricity-weighted total-output carbon intensity was approximately 314 gCO2 kWh−1, compared with a US total-output average of approximately 348 gCO2 kWh−1. Our approach provides a facility-resolved attributional framework for assessing the carbon footprint of hyperscale data centres using plant-level electricity-generation and emissions data.

title: Two-dimensional material membranes with precisely tunable interlayer spacing from nanometre to submillimetre
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Precise and reversible control over ion channel size in membrane materials is crucial for realizing optimized device performance, but conventional approaches to channel regulation suffer from limited tunability, reversibility and precision. Here we report a deprotonation–ion coordination strategy for the precise, reversible modulation of interlayer spacing over five orders of magnitude in layered material membranes. The interlayer expansion is driven by electrostatic repulsion due to the deprotonation of intercalated cellulose nanofibers and is reversibly tunable via charge compensation through cation coordination. As a result, we achieve an unprecedented degree of structural tunability: porosity from 0% to 78%, interlayer spacing from 1.39 to 152,000 nm and membrane thickness from 43 to 5,400 μm. Our strategy enables on-demand performance customization with the same membrane platform. For example, a slight interlayer expansion (to 1.48 nm) boosts zinc-ion capacitance by 67% relative to non-expanded membranes; a 21,583-fold expansion (to ~30 μm) raises osmotic energy conversion power by 63%, and a 100,719-fold expansion (to ~140 μm) unlocks exceptional pressure sensing. These results establish a generalizable paradigm for nanometric microstructure engineering of various van der Waals materials.

title: Controlling the flow of information in optical metrology
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Optical metrology has surpassed the Abbe–Rayleigh limit by leveraging nonlinear phenomena and statistical accumulation, and has recently unlocked subatomic precision using artificial intelligence estimators trained on measurand variations. Here we argue that further gains can be achieved by optimizing the flow of Fisher information carrying metrological content. We show that Fisher information flow need not follow the optical energy flow and that it exhibits resonance, diffraction and interference, singular points, and vorticity. It can exhibit a Talbot-like effect in which Fisher information density patterns repeat periodically with propagation distance, and it can be focused beyond the diffraction limit, mirroring the effect of optical superoscillation. Material composition, resonances, geometry and environment determine where information is generated, how it propagates, and how it can be enhanced and directed to improve precision. This perspective recasts metrology as information flow engineering, for applications ranging from atomic-scale diagnostics and smart manufacturing to remote sensing, radar and LiDAR.

title: Field‐Free Brightening of Dark Excitons in a Two‐Dimensional Perovskite by Organic Spacer Fluorination
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Modifying the organic spacer is a powerful way to tune the excitonic properties of two‐dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden–Popper (R–P) hybrid halide perovskites. Here, fluorination of the spacer, replacing phenylethylammonium (PEA) with 4‐fluorophenylethylammonium (4‐FPEA), is shown to brighten dark excitons in (4‐FPEA)
                    2
                    PbI
                    4
                    without an external magnetic field. Below 30 K, (4‐FPEA)
                    2
                    PbI
                    4
                    exhibits a sharp photoluminescence (PL) signal 7.8 meV below the bright exciton that is absent in (PEA)
                    2
                    PbI
                    4
                    . Its long lifetime, strong linear polarization, and quadratic magnetic‐field dependence identify this signal as dark‐exciton emission. A magnetic field of up to 0.7 T changes this emission only weakly, whereas it strongly brightens dark excitons in (PEA)
                    2
                    PbI
                    4
                    . The response is also asymmetric, with its minimum displaced from the zero field. This offset, absent in (PEA)
                    2
                    PbI
                    4
                    , points to a built‐in mixing of dark and bright states that acts as an internal field. Under two‐photon excitation, which generates excitons deep inside the crystal, the dark‐exciton emission persists. The brightening, therefore, originates in the bulk, unlike the surface‐related brightening reported for other 2D R–P perovskites. These results identify spacer fluorination as a simple chemical route to access spin‐forbidden excitonic states in 2D R–P perovskites.

title: Self‐Sustaining Lattice‐Oxygen Cycling Enables Durable Industrial‐Level Seawater Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lattice oxygen‐mediated seawater oxidation offers fast kinetics for energy‐efficient hydrogen production, but its practical application is hampered by catalyst degradation arising from transient oxygen vacancies and chloride corrosion at industrial current densities. Here we report an Ag‐decorated amorphous RuFeCo layered double hydroxide (Ag‐RuFeCo LDH) that enables self‐sustaining lattice‐oxygen cycling by integrating disorder‐activated lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) with an anion‐selective interface. Ru incorporation induces structural disorder and enhances Fe─O covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen participation in seawater oxidation. Meanwhile, oxophilic silver oxide reconstructed in situ establishes an OH
                    −
                    ‐enriched interfacial environment that mitigates Cl
                    −
                    adsorption and rapidly replenishes LOM‐generated oxygen vacancies, thereby stabilizing the catalyst structure. Consequently, Ag‐RuFeCo LDH requires only 308 mV overpotential to achieve 1.0 A cm
                    −2
                    in alkaline natural seawater and maintains stable performance during a cumulative operation exceeding 9500 h. An anion‐exchange‐membrane electrolyzer using Ag‐RuFeCo LDH as both electrodes reaches 1.0 A cm
                    −2
                    at 1.92 V and operates continuously for 1000 h with a low energy consumption of 4.59 kWh Nm
                    −3
                    H
                    2
                    . This strategy successfully overcomes the corrosion bottleneck of LOM in seawater electrolysis and offers a general strategy for durable and sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Remarkable Low‐Temperature Magnetocaloric Performance in a Frustrated Divalent Eu(II) Magnet Eu5FP3O12
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The development of
                    3
                    He‐free sub‐Kelvin adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration (ADR), which relies on the magnetocaloric (MC) effect in magnets, is constrained by the lack of magnetic refrigerants operating from several Kelvin to the milli‐Kelvin range. This work reports a geometrically frustrated divalent Eu(II)‐dominated magnet, Eu
                    5
                    FP
                    3
                    O
                    12
                    , designed by combining moderate magnetic frustration with a dense Eu(II) magnetic lattice, which is distinct from conventional trivalent Gd(III)‐based systems. Eu
                    5
                    FP
                    3
                    O
                    12
                    crystallizes in a hexagonal structure in which a subset of magnetic Eu(II) ions occupies a triangular lattice, giving rise to moderate magnetic frustration and a very low magnetic ordering temperature of 530 mK. Consequently, the Eu
                    5

                    3

                    3

title: Thermodynamically Controlled Multiphase Evolution in Single‐Crystal Cation‐Disordered Li‐Ion Cathode Materials
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Mn‐based disordered rock‐salt (Mn‐DRX) cathodes are promising materials for Li‐ion batteries, yet their application is limited by sluggish Li transport, voltage instability, and capacity fading. Here, we show that thermodynamic control of multiphase evolution from single‐crystal Mn‐DRX overcomes these limitations. Using grand‐potential phase diagrams with in situ and ex situ X‐ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy, we demonstrate that DRX composition and annealing conditions govern transformation into nanocomposites containing DRX, spinel, and monoclinic layered phases, with anatase formation predicted in specific Li–Mn–Ti–O compositions. Oxidative annealing at 300–500°C induces decomposition pathways: Li‐deficient compositions form DRX–spinel (DS) nanocomposites, whereas Li‐rich compositions form DRX–spinel–monoclinic layered (DSM) architectures. Unlike DS materials, which exhibit lower first‐charge capacities than discharge capacities, the monoclinic phase in DSM nanocomposites enables substantially improved first‐charge Li extraction, critical for practical Li‐ion batteries. The DSM nanocomposites deliver reversible capacities approaching 300 mAh g
                    −1
                    and discharge specific energies exceeding 800 Wh kg
                    −1
                    , while their cycling stability can be substantially improved by using a highly concentrated electrolyte and restricting the voltage window. This work establishes thermodynamically guided multiphase engineering as a strategy for addressing transport and stability limitations in DRX cathodes.

title: Multiscale Characterizations Toward Energy Storage Carbon Materials From Precursors to Electrodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The sp
                    2
                    ‐hybridized carbon materials such as graphite, soft carbon, and hard carbon, are broadly used as anodes for alkali‐metal‐ion batteries owing to their stable and controllable microstructures. However, the inherent structural complexity and multi‐stage synthesis processes of carbon materials pose challenges to their comprehensive characterization, limiting a deeper structural understanding and performance improvement of carbon electrodes. This review establishes a comprehensive characterization framework for the multiscale understanding of carbon materials from their precursors to carbon electrodes. Because the structural features of carbon materials are largely inherited from their precursors, we first summarize the recent advances in the characterization of their molecular structures and pyrolysis behaviors. We then discuss advanced characterization techniques and corresponding analysis methods used to understand the multiscale structures of carbon materials, including particles, microcrystals, and pore structures. We further provide a comprehensive overview of static and real time characterization techniques for studying interfacial ion transport and bulk ion diffusion kinetics in carbon electrodes. On this basis, we draw a decision‐making framework for multiscale characterization to help readers quickly navigate from problem definition to characterization strategy. Finally, we provide future perspectives to facilitate the efficient scientific investigation and rational design of high‐performance carbon materials for alkali‐metal‐ion batteries.

title: Direct CO2 splitting using light-based catalysis and an oxygen reservoir
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
As the dominant anthropogenic greenhouse gas, the conversion of CO
                    2
                    into value-added products is vital for achieving a circular economy. CO
                    2

                    2

                    2

The oxygen can then be released from the ceria by flowing nitrogen under white light illumination, a process that can be repeated multiple times, restoring full photocatalytic activity. This demonstrates a practical and scalable strategy for efficient CO
                    2

title: Leptin Receptor+ cells create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis in the bone marrow by synthesizing CXCL14
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Leptin Receptor-expressing (LepR
                    +
                    ) stromal cells in the bone marrow are a critical source of growth factors for the maintenance of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and most restricted hematopoietic progenitors. An important unresolved question is whether they also regulate terminal differentiation in some hematopoietic cells. We found that bone marrow LepR
                    +
                    cells promote thrombopoiesis by synthesizing the chemokine CXCL14.
                    Cxcl14
                    -expressing LepR
                    +
                    cells extend fine processes that wrap around perisinusoidal megakaryocytes. Deletion of
                    Cxcl14
                    from LepR
                    +
                    cells did not significantly alter HSC function or most aspects of bone marrow hematopoiesis, including megakaryocyte generation; however, it significantly reduced the numbers of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes in the bone marrow and platelets in the blood, as well as platelet quality. Megakaryocytes from

                      fl/fl

CXCL14 promoted platelet formation by remodeling lipid metabolism in megakaryocytes, increasing fatty acid transporter expression and enabling megakaryocytes to take up more polyunsaturated fatty acids from circulation. A high fat diet rescued the formation of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes and platelets, as well as platelet function, in
                    
                      Lepr-cre; Cxcl14
                      fl/fl

                    +

title: The evolution and function of eukaryote-to-cyanobacteria horizontal gene transfer
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Prokaryote-to-eukaryote horizontal gene transfer (HGT) has emerged as a driver of eukaryotic evolution. In contrast, eukaryote-to-prokaryote HGT remains poorly characterized, limiting insight into how eukaryote-derived genes influence prokaryotic evolution and function. Here, we reconstructed a comprehensive and well-resolved phylogeny of 469 high-quality Cyanobacteria genomes spanning all orders. Leveraging this framework, we identified 204 candidate functionally diverse genes of eukaryotic origin in cyanobacteria, likely representing 59 putative transfer events, including 197 genes not previously documented. All 204 candidates were intronless, consistent with intron loss during their evolutionary history. Transcriptomics reveal that HGT-acquired genes are expressed at significantly higher levels than both genome-wide and functionally matched non-HGT-acquired genes, suggesting functional importance. Notably, 138 genes exhibited functional annotations absent from the host cyanobacteria. We further characterized a granule-bound starch synthase (GBSS) putatively acquired by
                    Crocosphaera
                    from an ancestral archaeplastid lineage, enabling starch synthesis that may facilitate energy storage for nocturnal nitrogen fixation. These findings reveal that eukaryote-to-prokaryote gene transfer is an underappreciated driver of cyanobacterial evolution and function, with broad implications for microbial ecology, functional adaptation, and cross-domain genetic exchange.

title: Peak water: Trends in decoupling regional and global water use
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Water use for human activities, including food and fiber production, energy generation, and residential, commercial, and industrial supply, has grown significantly over the past century, driven by rising populations, expanding economic activity, and changes in technologies and consumer demands. Traditional water planning has long assumed that the demand for water, like other resource demands, will grow in perpetuity, shaping infrastructure development, land-use decisions, and water-system investments. However, recent data and analysis challenge this assumption, suggesting that total water use in certain regions and sectors has peaked or even begun to decline, despite continued population and economic growth. This paper’s primary contribution is to reevaluate the status of “peak water” and decoupling based on observational and statistical data, as well as multimodel simulations. Data on global, national, and regional water withdrawals indicate that certain peak water-use levels are being reached and the paper discusses past, current, and projected demand estimates; potential drivers of observed water use reductions; and different strategies for managing and modeling water use in the future. These findings indicate that the long-presumed correlation between water-resource use, economic development, and human well-being can be decoupled and that models of water use should reflect this. Decoupling solutions must focus on efficiency technologies, regulatory water-use caps, environmental flow protections, and enhanced monitoring networks.
